questions: How many devices did you fabricate and measure, and how many showed high-field pockets? Table S1 lists four moiré junctions, but high-field maps appear for GH1 and GH2 only. Were GH3 and GH4 taken above 1 T?
Why were the others set aside? If GH3 and GH4 showed no pockets, or weren't measured, could the SI say so?
Which ranges did you measure beyond the ones shown? In particular, did you map the hole minibands (n/ns < -1) at high field, where Fig. 1c shows Fabry-Pérot oscillations in the supercurrent?

What does the second-best device or dataset look like? GH2 (Fig. S13) partly answers this; how were the cuts at n/ns ∼ 1.8 and 4.3 T in Fig. 2c chosen, and do other pockets give similar Ic(B) patterns?

How was the 3447 Ω series resistance calibrated, does it put the two-terminal quantum Hall plateaus in Fig. S3 at h/νe², and could you show Fig. 2a before subtraction? How was the 20 mS cutoff in Fig. S18 chosen?
Were the patterns in Fig. 2c and Fig. S13c reproduced on up and down field sweeps, and how much time passed between repeats?

Have you mapped the supercurrent distribution (the Dynes-Fulton analysis of Fig. S9) as a function of n/ns through the minibands and near the van Hove singularities? GH2's high-field periods of 1.7 to 2.0 mT sit close to its zero-field period; how do you read that?

Fig. 3e uses base-temperature 1/R as a proxy for superconductivity. Does the normal-state map at 200 nA bias (Fig. S14) track ⟨v²⟩ in Fig. 3d in the same way, since dispersive magnetic Bloch bands also raise normal-state conductance?
